findings.title: NPE in getCredentials for users not in storage map
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials the code does var myUser = getMyUser(user) and then dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check. getFederatedCredentialsStream calls this for every user, including local users never added to the map. When myUser is null this throws NullPointerException, breaking credential listing, login and account APIs for local users whenever the provider is installed.

findings.title: Federated recovery credential loses its stored ID
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel is built with createFromValues() from the stored credentialData, but the stored ID from myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() is never copied to the new model. Every call therefore returns a different random ID. Callers that later call removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()) use a non-existent ID, so deletion of an exhausted federated recovery credential silently fails and the old credential is never removed.

findings.title: Federated recovery code validation never consumes codes
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE the code only checks generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) and returns true. It never marks the used code as consumed or persists any state change, unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider which invalidates a code after use. Consequence: the same recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, getNextRecoveryAuthnCode never advances, and allCodesUsed never becomes true, defeating the single-use security property of recovery codes.

findings.title: disableCredentialType does not support recovery codes
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.disableCredentialType only clears myUser.otp for OTP types and logs unsupported for everything else. Federated recovery codes can therefore never be disabled or deleted through the standard disable path used by admin REST and account console. After all codes are used or when an admin disables the type, the federated recovery credential remains in the map and stays valid.

findings.title: Exhausted federated credential removed with local-only API
findings.body: In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid the code loads the credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential which now prefers federated storage, but on allCodesUsed it always calls removeStoredCredentialById(id). That API removes a locally stored credential; federated credentials must be removed via the user-storage disable/remove path. For a federated recovery credential the call does nothing, so an exhausted credential is left in user storage while only adding the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() causes 500 when credential missing or exhausted
findings.body: In RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean the constructor does credentialModelOpt.get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without isPresent checks. If the user has no recovery credential or all codes are already used, this throws NoSuchElementException during login page rendering, producing a 500 error instead of a handled authentication failure or required-action redirect.

findings.title: Recovery storage test does not verify single-use or removal
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin the test only sets up codes and logs in once with code 0. Unlike the OTP tests it never verifies that the used code is consumed, that reuse is rejected, that exhaustion triggers re-setup, or that disable/delete via admin/account APIs clears federated storage. The replay and deletion bugs above therefore pass undetected.
